title: What are all mechanisms to resolve multiple beans of the same type (@Primary, @Qualifier, variable name, List/Map injection, @Profile, custom qualifier)? When does NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException occur? What is the difference between @Primary and @Qualifier?
shortTitle: How do you resolve multiple beans of the same type?
keyPoints: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException occurs when Spring finds multiple beans of the same type and cannot decide which one to inject.
@Qualifier on the injection point explicitly names the bean to inject and has the highest priority.
@Primary on the bean definition marks it as the default when no qualifier is specified.
@Qualifier overrides @Primary: if both exist, the explicit qualifier wins.
List<T> injection gets all beans of type T; Map<String, T> injection maps bean names to instances for runtime selection.
Field or parameter name matching the bean name acts as an implicit qualifier.
Custom qualifier annotations like @PrimaryChannel provide type-safe, self-documenting disambiguation.

s1_definition.oneliner: @Primary marks the default bean when no qualifier is specified; @Qualifier explicitly picks a specific bean by name; @Qualifier always overrides @Primary; List/Map injection gets all beans of the type.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException** -- the exception Spring throws when it finds multiple beans of the same type and no mechanism resolves the ambiguity.
- **@Qualifier** -- placed on the injection point (constructor parameter, field, or setter) to explicitly name which bean to inject; highest priority.
- **@Primary** -- placed on the bean definition to mark it as the default when no qualifier is specified; lower priority than @Qualifier.
- **List/Map injection** -- `List<T>` injects all beans of type T; `Map<String, T>` maps bean names to instances for runtime selection.
- **Custom qualifier** -- a user-defined annotation like `@PrimaryChannel` that provides type-safe disambiguation without relying on string bean names.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India has three notification channels: email, SMS, and push. When the TransferService asks for "a NotificationService," Spring sees three candidates and panics (NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException). @Primary marks email as the default because most services want email. @Qualifier("sms") explicitly picks SMS for the fraud alert service that needs urgent delivery. List injection gets ALL channels for the marketing broadcaster that sends to every channel at once.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Resolution Priority (highest to lowest):

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1. @Qualifier("beanName")             │  explicit pick
  │       │                                │
  │       ▼                                │
  │  2. @Primary                           │  default fallback
  │       │                                │
  │       ▼                                │
  │  3. Parameter/field name match         │  implicit match
  │       │                                │
  │       ▼                                │
  │  4. Single candidate                   │  only one exists
  │       │                                │
  │       ▼                                │
  │  NONE → NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException│
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Injection Patterns:

  TransferService ──→ @Primary (email)     │ default
  FraudAlertService ─→ @Qualifier (sms)    │ explicit
  MarketingService ──→ List<all channels>  │ broadcast
  PreferenceService ─→ Map<name, channel>  │ runtime pick
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When Spring finds multiple beans of the same type, it throws NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException unless you tell it which one to use. The resolution mechanisms in priority order are: @Qualifier on the injection point which explicitly names the bean, @Primary on the bean definition which marks the default, parameter or field name matching a bean name as an implicit qualifier, and single-candidate resolution when only one bean exists. @Qualifier always overrides @Primary.

In the National Bank of India notification gateway, Rajesh has three NotificationService implementations: email (marked @Primary because most services want email), SMS, and push. The TransferService receives the @Primary email bean automatically for transfer confirmations. The FraudAlertService uses @Qualifier("smsNotificationService") to explicitly request SMS for urgent security alerts that need immediate delivery. The MarketingBroadcastService injects a List of all NotificationService beans to broadcast promotions through every channel simultaneously. The CustomerPreferenceService injects a Map keyed by bean name and selects the channel at runtime based on Priya's saved preference in the database, avoiding if-else chains entirely.

Adding a new notification channel, such as WhatsApp, requires only creating a new @Service class that implements NotificationService. The List and Map injections pick it up automatically. No existing code changes are needed. For type-safe disambiguation without fragile string names, Pankaj recommends custom qualifier annotations like @PrimaryChannel and @UrgentChannel, where a typo is a compile error instead of a runtime failure.

Remember one sentence: @Primary marks the default bean, @Qualifier explicitly picks a specific one, and @Qualifier always wins when both are present.
